definitions.explanation: A deliberately untrue statement. A formal word implying intentional deception, often used in legal, medical, or serious contexts.

examples.japanese: {虚言|きょげん}を{弄|ろう}する。
{彼|かれ}の{証言|しょうげん}は{虚言|きょげん}だと{判明|はんめい}した。
examples.english: His testimony was found to be a lie.

examples.japanese: {虚言|きょげん}{癖|へき}のある{人|ひと}は、{自分|じぶん}でも{嘘|うそ}と{本当|ほんとう}の{区別|くべつ}がつかなくなることがある。
examples.english: People with a tendency to lie may eventually lose the ability to distinguish their own lies from the truth.

notes:
A formal, literary word for lying. Composed of {虚|きょ} (empty, false) + {言|げん} (words, speech). More severe in tone than the everyday word {嘘|うそ}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {虚言|きょげん}を{弄|ろう}する: to utter falsehoods (formal)
- {虚言|きょげん}{癖|へき}: a habit of lying; pathological lying
- {虚言|きょげん}{症|しょう}: mythomania, pathological lying (clinical term)
- {虚言|きょげん}を{吐|は}く: to tell lies

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {嘘|うそ}: lie — the standard everyday word; used in all registers from casual to formal
- {偽|いつわ}り: falsehood, deception — literary; implies deliberate deception with a broader scope than just words
- {虚偽|きょぎ}: falsehood, untruth — formal/legal; often used for false documents or statements ({虚偽|きょぎ}{申告|しんこく}: false declaration)

USAGE:
Do not confuse with the homophone {狂言|きょうげん}, which refers to a traditional Japanese comedic theater form. The readings are close but the pitch accent and kanji are different.
